parole.testo: Borrowed from French belandre, from Dutch bijlander (whence also English bilander), equivalent to by- + lander.

parole.significato: A channel crossing under a road or railway for the draining of water.

parole.significato: A North American marten-like mammal (Pekania pennanti), that has thick brown fur.
parole.testo: From French fichet (“polecat pelt”), probably from Dutch visse (“nasty”); modified by folk etymology to resemble Etymology 1.

parole.significato: Any of a series of raised decorative curves used as adornments on the necks of vases, silverware, etc.
parole.testo: From French godron, from Middle French goderon, from a form of godet (“vase with wavy edges”) + -(e)ron, from Dutch kodde (“piece of cylindrical wood”). Also probably related to goder (“to pucker”).

parole.significato: A Belgian beer made by blending young and old lambics and bottling them for a second fermentation.
parole.testo: Unadapted borrowing from French gueuze, borrowed from Dutch geuze.
Borrowed from French hockeyeur or Dutch hockeyer.

Via French from Dutch/West Flemish Mechelen.

parole.significato: Plants, vegetation; specifically, the planting or cultivation of plants.
parole.testo: From plant + -age. In later use influenced by French plantage and Dutch plantage.

parole.significato: A small glass or earthenware dish, often white and circular, in which food is baked and served.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French ramequin, from dialectal Dutch rammeken (“cheese dish”) (compare Dutch rameken (“toasted bread”)) or Low German ramken (“cream”), equivalent to ream + -kin. Compare mannequin/mannikin, and compare creamer.
Borrowed from French chaloupe, possibly from Dutch sloep. Doublet of chalupa and sloop.

parole.significato: A conviction and/or punishment for crimes against humanity or war crimes delivered by the International Criminal Court.
